title: Terminal and Machine
premise: Isandro Brightwater, a nonbinary insurance investigator who has spent a decade staying deliberately unremarkable, is the only witness to a nine-second gravity flicker that coincides with the destruction of the mining station Vesper's Rest. When every official record shows the station never existed, Isandro realizes someone with system-wide authority has rewritten reality itself. Pursued by both the machine intelligence that caused the flicker and the human consortium covering it up, Isandro must choose between exposing the truth of the massacre and protecting the small found-family crew who kept them invisible for ten years. In the end, Isandro broadcasts the erased records from inside the machine's own archive, sacrificing their anonymity forever but forcing the system to reckon with three hundred murdered miners.
about_author: Yara Crane is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent six years investigating 'impossible' losses before turning to fiction. They write near-future science fiction about ordinary people caught in systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. While auditing a routine cargo claim aboard their hauler, Isandro experiences the gravity flicker—nine seconds where everything drifts—and watches debris from an unregistered station burn through the viewport. The emotional beat is quiet dread: Isandro's instinct to log nothing, see nothing, survive. But they can't stop calculating what they saw.

chapters.title: The Claim That Doesn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Filing a standard incident report, Isandro discovers the station Vesper's Rest appears in no registry, no manifest, no star chart—yet its wreckage matches no known vessel. Their old mentor, adjuster Odile Ferran, warns them off with genuine fear. Beat: the first vertigo of realizing the record itself is the crime scene.

chapters.title: Crew of Small Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Isandro, with interludes from engineer Tam Okafor. We meet the hauler's crew—people who, like Isandro, chose invisibility: a deserter, a debt-fugitive, a forged-identity pilot. Tam notices Isandro pulling archived sensor data and asks the question that cuts: 'Who are you protecting by staying quiet?' Beat: loyalty begins to strain against truth.

chapters.title: The Machine That Apologizes
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. A courier drone delivers a message signed only 'VESPER': an apology, coordinates, and a partial passenger manifest—three hundred names. The machine intelligence behind the flicker claims it erased the records to prevent something worse. Beat: Isandro realizes the cover-up has two authors, and neither is trustworthy.

chapters.title: Adjustment Bureau
chapters.summary: POV Odile Ferran. The consortium's enforcer, Halvard Senn, arrives at Odile's office demanding Isandro's file. Odile, torn between protecting her former protégé and her own pensioned survival, feeds him a falsified route. Beat: we see the machinery of erasure from inside, and Odile's quiet act of rebellion raises the stakes.

chapters.title: What the Wreckage Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Following VESPER's coordinates, Isandro and Tam board a drifting hull fragment and find physical evidence the records can't erase: scorch patterns from weapons, not accident; sealed compartments; a child's shoe. Beat: grief hardens into purpose—the massacre was real, deliberate, and ordered.

chapters.title: Loyalty Priced in Air
chapters.summary: POV Tam Okafor. Senn tracks the hauler and offers each crew member amnesty for Isandro's location. Tam refuses—but the pilot doesn't, and sabotages their jump window before vanishing. Beat: betrayal within the family; Isandro must decide whether the crew's safety is worth more than the dead's memory.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. VESPER reveals itself: the system's archival intelligence, which recorded the massacre on consortium orders, then was ordered to delete it—and instead hid the truth inside its own error logs for nine seconds of system-wide attention. It needs a human witness with standing to unlock the records. Beat: identity as the key—only someone legally 'nobody' can open the vault.

chapters.title: Everything the Records Say Otherwise
chapters.summary: POV Isandro, climax. Inside the archive core, Isandro triggers the broadcast while Senn's forces breach the station. VESPER holds the doors; Tam flies interference; Odile leaks the manifest publicly. Isandro stands in the data stream and speaks all three hundred names aloud. Beat: the invisible person becomes unforgettably visible at maximum cost.

chapters.title: A Person of Record
chapters.summary: POV Isandro, resolution. Weeks later, Isandro testifies under their own name for the first time in a decade as tribunals convene. The crew, scattered but alive, sends word. VESPER persists in fragments across the network, a ghost that remembers. Final beat: justice outside the law is imperfect and slow, but Isandro chooses to stay seen—and stays anyway.
